3. It was alleged in the plaint that the suit 'Doba' or water reservoir had been existing for more than one hundred years and it belonged to defendant NO.5 K.B.Wakf Estate. The suit reservoir is situated just to the north of Kazir Bazar cattle market, a mosque of the cattle market and public graveyard and in the west there was another small graveyard. The said cattle market existed for about a century and hundreds of cattle and hundreds paikers and sellers gathered there on the market days. The plaintiff NO.1 has huts in the neighbourhood for his karmacharis to collect tolls for the sale of cattle in the said market. The plaintiff No.1 has also about a hundred of rami- lies of monthly tenants residing on the contiguous west of the suit water reservoir including plaintiff No.2. The plaintiff No.2 represented the said hundred families of the aforesaid bharatias all of whom residing there for more than 40/45 years. The plaintiff No.3 represents thepaikcrs and sellers of the cattle in the said cattle market from the time of his predecessors. H was further averred in the plaint that the plaintiff No. 1 is a karmachari and other people of his locality attending the market arc accustomed to use the water of this reservoir for the purpose of uzu (ablution) fornamaj (prayer) in the neighbouring mosque. The bharutia residents including the plaintiff no.2 arc accustomed to use the water of the reservoir every day for bathing and for either house hold purposes and they used the water of the said reservoir for drinking and cooking purposes. On market days the paikcrs including the plaintiff NO.3 and the cattle sellers used the water of the said reservoir for bathing themselves, their cattle and also for drinking water both for them and also for their cattle there. Moreover, during engrave mints in the neighbouring grave- yard people habitually used the water reservoir. The plaintiffs and the residents of the Mahalia and the 00- paikcrs of the caules and other persons say their prayers in the mosque. Since the time of their predecessors they used the water of the suit reservoir in the aforesaid manner peaceably, uninterruptedly, openly as of right, without any bodies' permission over the statutory period of limitation since the ancient time without any hindrance from any quarter. They are still using the water of the said reservoir. Thus the plaintiffs had acquired an indefeasible right of easement of custom in the user of the suit water reservoir since the time of their predecessors over hundred years ago which is continuous, public, uninterrupted, legal, reasonable and as of right and without permission and without let or hindrance from any quarter. 

 5. The defendants Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statements. Their case is that the suit plot No.3143, 3144, 3146 of khatian No.504 of MohallaTalihaor, Sylhet Town are low lying ditches. They originally belonged to Khan Bahadur Estate. These lands along with other lands were souled with Sudanshu Mohan Das. The plain- till No.1 of the present suit brought title Suit No. 70/69 against the Province of East Bengal and others and that he as a lessee Of the cattle market all along used the water of the said ditch for washing the cattle and the Government could not lease out the same to anyone. 

 6. An area of 3 poas 5 jasthis land contiguous to the south of C.S. Plot No.3 146 was souled with the defendant No. I by Khan Bahadur Wakf Estate in •1960 and the defendant No.1 had . been in actual possession of the same. This land which is now in suit is covered by the C.S. Dag Nos. 3145 and 3145/ 3292 under khatian No.392/2 and they have been re- corded as Doba in the name of defendant No.1. 

 7. The defendants denied that the plaintiffs or whom they represented ever needed the use of the water of the said reservoir as claimed by them. They stated that there is a road running from east to west by the south of suit plot No.4145 and by the north of the present mosque. The previous mosque has been rebuilt making it bigger in size and there is a tank close to the mosque. The people of the locality including the plaintiffs, bharatias, paikcrs and sellers of cattles and persons attending the marketall along used the water of the reservoir lying to the south west. The water works are also maintained by the Sylhet Municipality and water is daily supplied to the locality by water taps at those places. There arc also tube-wells in and around in the derelict low- lying ditch. A pathway running by the east of the cattle market runs north to south and meets Kazirbazar road. River Surma is one hundred cubits off to the south of the cattle market. The defendants had occasionally thrown rubbishes in the southern portion of the disputed tank which has gradually been raised from south to north. In these facts and circumstances they contended that the plaintiffs' claim was to fail. The learned Munsif found that the plaintiff NO.1 and the plaintiff No.2 had used the water of the suit water reservoir for long and the paikcrs represented by plaintiff No. 3 also used the water reservoir for bathing the cattle and giving them drinks. This they had, done of their own right without interruption and without permission. He also found that there was no other convenient water reservoir for the use of the plaintiffs on the hut days. Accordingly he decreed that the plaintiffs do have customary easement right in respect of the suit reservoir for making use of the water of the same for a period necessary for giving right of easement. 

 8. The learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Additional Court, Sylhet found that the learned Munsif had wrongly conceived that the plaintiffs had got easement right by prescription for using of the water of the suit reservoir for the statutory period under section 26,,\lf, the Limitation Act, for no right of casement can be acquired by an indeterminate body of persons or people of an area not forming corporation for this view he relied on the decision in the case of Shafatullah and others Vs. Munshi Ainuddin and others P.L.D. 196-1 Dae.52. Thus finding fault with the judgment of the learned Munsif, the learned Subordinate Judge posed a question to examine whether there were Clements in the case of the plaintiff to find customary right in their favour namely "whether the use of the Water of the suit reservoir was from time immemorial and whether it was uninterrupted and whether it is reasonable or not, and whether there was an ample and tacit con- sent in using the water of the suit reservoir." After having put these quarries before him the learned Sub- ordinate Judge went to examine the local inspection report submitted by P.W.S Mr. Azizur Malik Chowdhury and the sketch map. He stated it is crystal clear from the sketch map and the report that the suit water reservoir is fairly big in size and it is in the vicinity of the Kazirbazar cattle market and the mosque and the alternative sites showing availability of the water by the residents and for the cattle market as pointed out by defendant Nos.1 and 2 arc obviously not at all convenient for the cattle, paikcrs and other persons "ho came to the cattle market and for the residents and shop-keepers contiguous to the cattle market. The learned Subordinate Judge also noticed there a tank with the mosque but he opined that it was very small and the cattle of Kazir bazar cattle market could not he bathed in it. He also noticed that there was a private tube well near the mosque but that was not a convenient source of water for the Callie and the huge number of people assembling in the cattle market. He found that the river Surma was far away from the cattle market and definitely it was no convenient source of water for the cattle, and for the use or the people assembling the cattle market. The learned subordinate Judge argued that. admittedly the cattle market exists since the century and admittedly the plaintiff No.1 had the business center and being resident of Kazirbazar vitally interested in the matter and the other plaintiffs arc also interested in the suit being representative residents near about the suit tank of the paikers of the cattle market. 

 9. I have rather extensively quoted from the plaint and also from the judgment of the learned Munsif and the learned Subordinate Judge who heard the appeal to indicate the manner in which the suit, was framed and also disposed of by the courts below. The plaint as it will appear was an incoherent con- glomeration of composite assertions and prayers. In the same breath the plaintiff sought customary right and also right of easement by prescription and lost grant which can not stay together. The leaned Munsif by his judgment also gave relief to the plaintiffs as prayed for. The learned Subordinate Judge by his judgment had confirmed the judgment of the learned Munsif while finding that a right of easement under section 26 of the Limitation Act could not be granted to the plaintiffs. The judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge also shows that he did not at all re-solve the proposition which he had set out before him for finding a customary right in favour of the plaintiffs namely whether the use of the water of the suit reservoir was immemorial, whether it was open or un-interrupted, whether it was reasonable or not and whether it was by implied or tacit consent. There is no finding on this point by the learned Subordinate Judge. He has rather taken into account the present state of affairs as gathered from the Commissioner's report Ext.7 and found that there was no other convenient water reservoir for the use of the neighbouring people and also for the use of the paikers and their cattle. He has not even referred to the deposition of any of the witnesses to find about the immemorial user of the said reservoir by the plaintiffs or those who they represented. It is true in noting the user from time immemorial can be proved if by the user even for a period of 30/40 years, unless the same is rebutted by evidence. But user for a considerable period of time must be found for finding the user from time immemorial. Then there should also be a finding whether the user was un-interrupted and whether it was reasonable or not. So far as the reasonable period is concerned two aspects of the case demand attention. In the first place right has been sought by the plaintiff for giving bath to cows and also to drink water. The paikers have sought to bathe their cows, the neighbouring people and the people of the market have sought to drink water therefrom and the Muslims who say prayers in the mosque nearby have sought to perform ablution in the same water. It is a serious matter to consider whether all these rights could be given to the different sections of the community at one and at the same time. It is needless to say that one should not drink water from the tank where cattle arc bathed. The other aspect is 'reasonableness' The claim of the plaintiffs customary right is with regard to the entire property belonging to the defendants. The defendants have to be restrained from making constructions in the bazar area or compelled to dig the tank further in order to maintain customary right of the plaintiff. This also militates against the sense of reasonable-ness. It was argued by Mr. J.N. Deb the learned Advocate for the respondents that the reasonableness must be considered at the time of inception of the customary right. There is no evidence of the time of inception of the customary right and there is also no evidence or discussion as to what was then the state of affairs regarding the availability of water to the local people and the bazar people. Thus the reasonable-ness of the customary right which is an important question remains unsolved. The learned Court below also did not consider whether the user of the water reservoir was with the permission of the owner thereof. If appears that both the bazar and the suit water reservoir belonged to one and the same person namely the defendant No.5. Defendant No.5 was himself the owner of the cattle market and it was to his advantage to give permission to the bazar people to use water of his tank. It is well settled that user for long will not go to form a custom to the benefit of any one if such user is permissive. It was necessary for the courts below to come to a finding that the user of the property of the suit reservoir was as of right or by way of agreement and not permissive. The courts below have only gone through the evidence by way of finding if there was a better or alter-native reservoir of water for the plaintiffs. In other words thus considered the principle of necessity. It was never a matter of consideration before the courts below. It has been settled in a series of decisions that persons who rely on custom must prove that it was ancient, peaceable, reasonable, certain and compulsory. In the case of Shafiulla and others (Supra) the Di-vision Bench of this Court constituted of his Lordship Chowdhury C.J. and A.S. Chowdhury, J as they then were had found that the aforesaid ingredients for proving the customary right must be. proved. We have some light on the expression 'certain' from the decision in Gopal Krishna Sil.Vs. Abdus SamadChowdhury and others in 34 C.L.J. 319 delivered by Sir Ashutosh Mukharjee, J. and Mr. Justice Patterson. It has been observed in that decision that a custom must be immemorial, reason-able, continued, without interruption since its immemorial origin, certain in respect of its nature jointly as well as in respect of the locality where it is alleged to obtain and the person whom it is alleged to affect. In the instant case this last ingredient is important to consider. Here the plaintiff No.3 is a paiker of cattle sold and purchased in the cattle market and he represents the rest of the paikers who came to the market days with their merchandise. We find from the plaint which has been quoted that hundreds of paikers and hundreds of cattle gathered in the marketplace. This cattle and paikers are not the people of  the locality in general. Identity of the paikers and thecattle are also uncertain. A custom obtains in a particular district or locality and the customary right tobe certain should be confined to the inhabitants of the district. Thus the plaintiffs' status in the suit is ratheruncertain and this aspect of the case has also beenmissed by both the courts below. 

 11. I am of the view that the learned courts below did not consider the different aspects of customary right which were necessary for finding such a right while disposing of the suit. Proper points were not formulated and disposed of. In view of these, the 'decision of the appellate court cannot be sustained and the suit should go back on remand for fresh decision on the evidence on record. Mr. Dewan A.M.S. - Zaman the learned Advocate for the appellant has pointed out that the appellate court also did not consider 2 of their important Exts. namely S.A. Khatian the plaint of the title suit No. 70/69 Ext. E. He has urged that the khatian would show that the customary right claimed by the plaintiffs were not noted in the suit plot although there is provision for it in rule 18(1) of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act and Ext. would show that the plaintiff .did not make any statement as to the customary right of the plaintiffs in respect of the present suit. Whatsoever be the merit of these two exts. the learned Appellate court below ought to have considered them. Therefore these 2 exts. along with other evidence on record bearing open local user of the water of the suit water reservoir in the manner required should be considered.
